name: SHT35 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Sensirion high-accuracy digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.1 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±1.5 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface (SHT3x-DIS family). Runs on 2.15–5.5 V. Sold as: Seeed Studio Grove - I2C High Accuracy Temp&Humi Sensor (SHT35) (101020592; 4-pin Grove I2C connector SCL, SDA, VCC, GND with 10 kΩ pull-ups on board), I2C address 0x45 (0x44 with the ADDR jumper re-soldered to GND).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is, very accurately.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (Grove pin 1, yellow wire; 10 kΩ pull-up on board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (Grove pin 2, white wire; 10 kΩ pull-up on board)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V or 5 V (chip 2.15–5.5 V; Grove pin 3, red wire)

supplierQuery: Seeed Grove I2C High Accuracy Temp Humi Sensor SHT35 101020592
buildNotes: The board has a 2 mm Grove socket, not 0.1 in pins: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable (yellow SCL, white SDA, red VCC, black GND).
Default I2C address is 0x45 because the ADDR jumper is bridged to VCC; cut that trace and bridge to GND for 0x44 (e.g. for a second sensor).
Single-shot command 0x24 0x00 then wait at least 15.5 ms before reading 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC.
Check each CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Keep the sensor away from the board's regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air around them.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sht35 import SHT35

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = SHT35(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
